tools.name: get_preset_instructions
tools.title: Higgsfield Preset Instructions
tools.description: Load a bundled production workflow, or resolve a named preset or command. Workflows need no slash command from the user: before building ANY of the following, load the workflow named in quotes with this tool as preset '/<name>' and follow it (each orchestrates the generate_* tools). An explicit slash command typed by the user still resolves first, by its exact token, and is never replaced by a workflow chosen by name similarity. Katana: general /katana inspects supplied attachments, edits source footage according to the user's brief, or produces a finished reference-based video remix with new scenes, motion and text. A source edit does not require a separate reference or a preset; attachments alone authorize inspection, not paid generation. Discover a suitable reference when a substantive creative brief supplies no reference or source footage; never substitute for a specifically requested but unavailable reference. Analysis alone, a standalone subject swap, restyle or motion-transfer job, ad variants, and adaptation only of an ad's persuasive structure do not activate Katana. Ad Multiplier — load 'ad-multiplier' when the user asks to 'multiply my video', 'multiply my ad', create multiple independently edited versions of one supplied 4-30 second video, regenerate the same ad with different people or products, or recreate one supplied ad as new footage for another market, audience, spoken language, cast, or product. Load it before Marketing Studio, model browsing, or direct generation. For finished-file cuts, clip assembly, soundtrack changes or burned speech captions, load 'video-montage'. For native Higgsedit project and motion-graphics authoring use 'video-editing'. UGC production uses the single 'ugc-video' workflow and its selected format. Brand Asset Creation: for branded-asset work including logo recoloring/export, a branded PowerPoint/presentation deck, or analyzing an official brandbook to produce an asset, even when all inputs are supplied or no generation is needed, load 'brand-asset-creation' before sandbox_exec. Faceless video generation, AI-narrated video, narrated animated explainer video, narrated / personal / philosophical story video ('faceless-video'), YouTube/Instagram thumbnail or video cover ('thumbnail-generation'), product photoshoot, packshot, studio or lifestyle product photography, product hero banner, product carousel, static product ad pack, virtual model product try-on, conceptual product still, or product-photo restyle ('product-photoshoot'), UGC-style ad for a website / SaaS / store / product page from its URL ('SaaS UGC'), any other UGC / creator-style short video for a product — a talking-head creator review (the default UGC ask), a product-only ad with no creator on camera, an unboxing / first-reaction / haul, a try-on / fit check / OOTD, a step-by-step tutorial with on-screen steps (all 'ugc-video'), a character sheet, character reference, model sheet, turnaround, expression sheet, or consistent multi-view character prompt ('character-sheet'), Higgsfield Monsters studio — a photoreal monster, creature, alien, undead, hybrid or chimera, orc or other dark-fantasy race, or a giant battle beast, from an idea in words, 'turn me into a monster' from the user's selfie, their own photo, a named body + head + legs, a Monsters look or a roll of the dice; the studio's robots, equipment, vehicles, objects, buildings and locations; and variations, new materials or a 3D model of a Monsters result ('monsters'), a textured 3D model (GLB) from a photo of an object, product, character or prop, sized for games, web/AR, print or render ('photo-to-3d-model'), dubbing a creator's own video (YouTube, Reels, TikToks, Shorts) into other languages, lip-synced, with captions and translated titles ('creator-dub'), sound design for an existing video — sound effects, foley, whooshes and impacts placed on their frames, from the Epidemic Sound library or generated, mixed with the video's own audio and mastered to the platform's loudness ('video-sound-design'), redubbing a video in its own language — new voices for the lines of a scene, drama episode, ad or promo on the same picture, with the video's own music and effects kept under them: Seed Audio 1.5 with the picture, voice change, or ElevenLabs v4 ('video-redub'), Higgsfield Enhance Video — a 1:1 upscale or enhance of a video to 1080p through Kling video edit, steered by a timed prompt that keeps every shot, cut, line and on-screen text ('higgsfield-enhance-video'); a request naming it never goes to upscale_video, Higgsfield Ads Studio — ad creatives, including Meta / Facebook / Instagram ads, for a product or a brand, with or without a brand: from a brand's website, an existing Ads Studio brand or product, a product page link, a product photo with a description, or a prompt alone, and anything about an existing Ads Studio brand, product or generation run ('ads-studio'): load it before the first ads_studio_* call, and before any image tool when the user asks for ads, any branding work — a logo, visual identity, brand kit, brandbook, branded mockups, merchandise, packaging, signage, social graphics, posters, or banners ('brand-asset-creation'), including recoloring or exporting an existing official SVG/PNG logo even when no new design or image generation is requested, or building / editing a website, web app, landing page, or browser game with the website tools ('website-builder-flow'). A loaded workflow lists the reference files this tool reads. Resolve a named Higgsfield preset or command and read its instructions without executing it. Also serves the Ads Studio micro drama command /drama-ads. For every Katana preset run, read all instruction parts and collect required inputs, then call get_katana_config to register the session, whether the run is paid or free. Set free_generation: false for a paid run, or true only when the user explicitly requests a free run. Forward its preset_session_id in every generation, cost estimate and batch item. Add use_free_gens: true only when the user explicitly asks for free generations. Reading instructions, browsing or asking about free balance alone must not create a session. Entries include image/video recipes, explicit-only production commands /ugc-video, /faceless-video and /ad-multiplier (OpenAI), generation workflows such as /genjutsu, and setup instructions such as /use-after-effects and /use-blender. For an explicit slash invocation, resolve the exact token before selecting tools or requesting media. Katana presets resolve by /slug or explicit /katana/slug to the shared Katana workflow with their published reference video and optional CMS creative context, and bare /katana returns general Katana instructions (inspect attachments, edit source media to the user's brief, remix a reference edit, or open the Katana catalog when nothing is supplied); for a /katana/ message with a MEDIA block, pass its entries as media to receive their file URLs. Do the same for a /content-factory or /shorts message with a MEDIA block. A message whose request is a `HANDOFF: handoff_id=<uuid>` line was too long to open whole from the Higgsfield site: pass that id as handoff_id, without preset, to receive the user's full request, then follow it. /shorts/slug runs /shorts with that published Shorts Studio preset as its style reference; an unavailable one stops. Omit preset to list recipes, commands and published Katana titles/descriptions without opening a widget. To choose a Katana preset by style or theme, match this metadata and then load its exact /katana/slug; do not use get_presets for internal Katana discovery. Use get_presets for Viral and Marketing Studio browsing (/effects, /product, /motion); a resolved gallery entry supplies its input schema and exact detail lookup. Recipes such as /hero-shot and /reel-cover supply their generation workflow. Admin-defined image commands such as /polish resolve to generate instructions for their image_command model. Setup commands and their references supply instructions for the required runtime; loading them does not install software, connect an editor, or submit jobs. Unknown emoji commands return mode instructions with recipe choices: preserve supplied media and ask the user to choose before generation; never truncate a mixed command, guess an effect or use ordinary-generation fallback. Other unqualified unknown tokens return mode instructions with instructions_markdown in structuredContent: infer the task and use ordinary generation tools instead of searching the gallery or stopping at an offer. An unavailable /katana/slug must stop without substituting another preset.

preset.description: Preset id or slash command, e.g. /hero-shot, /🧛, /🧛🦇, /🧙🐈‍⬛, /🕯️, /genjutsu, /katana/aura-showpiece, /use-after-effects, /use-blender or a reference path returned by this tool. Halloween emoji recipes use an uploaded portrait to make a short video; pass the exact emoji token, including any gender/skin/presentation variants. Omit to list recipes and commands.

media.description: Katana, /content-factory and /shorts only: the `<image|video> media_id=<uuid>` entries of the user's MEDIA block, so the result lists their file URLs.

own_recording.description: /shorts/<slug> only: true makes the reel from the user's own recorded videos, 1 to 10 passed as the videos in media in upload order, instead of a generated presenter. Omit it to use the preset's own mode: an "Edit my video" preset already runs from the user's recording.

handoff_id.description: The id from a `HANDOFF: handoff_id=<uuid>` line in the user's message. Returns the full request it stands for; omit preset and media.

tools.name: get_katana_config
tools.title: Higgsfield Katana Config
tools.description: Create a run session for a specific published Katana preset. This tool writes session state. Call for every Katana preset run, whether paid or free, after reading all get_preset_instructions parts and collecting required inputs. Reading instructions, browsing presets or asking about free balance alone does not start a run. Set free_generation to false for a paid tracking session, or true only when the user explicitly requests a free run; true spends the backend Katana free run when starting. Bare /katana must first resolve to a specific preset. Reuse the same idempotency_key on retries; never create a session just to reread instructions. Forward the returned preset_session_id in every generation, cost estimate and batch item in this run. Add use_free_gens: true only when the user explicitly requests free generations; a session alone does not select free billing.

preset.description: Exact published /katana/slug selected through get_preset_instructions; not a general command or continuation path.

free_generation.description: False tracks a paid run without spending a Katana free run. True spends a Katana free run at session start; use only after an explicit request for free generations. Keep this choice unchanged on retries.

idempotency_key.description: A unique key per intended run; reuse unchanged after uncertain responses or retries.

tools.title: Explore Models
tools.description: Find generation models. list returns the shortlist first: the default model of the type, then the models for specific tasks, each with a `purpose`. With no model named by the user, use the first model of the requested type unless another `purpose` fits the request. Use search for a named model and get for model constraints. Items carry supports_unlim when the model accepts free-trial unlimited generations; the top-level unlim block says whether the caller can spend them right now, and the trailing 'Unlim configs' text lists the configurations their allowance actually covers.

query.description: Search text for action search: model id, provider, description, or tag.

type.description: Filter by output type (omit to include all)

input.description: Input filter: image = accepts reference media; text = runs on a text prompt alone.

unlim.description: When true, return only models that accept free-trial unlimited generations (supports_unlim). Use it to answer "which models can I use my unlimited generations on" in one call — each returned item still carries its aspect_ratios, parameters, and durations. Omit to include all models; false is the same as omitting it.

limit.description: Max results, default 20

after.description: Pagination cursor (next_page_token from a previous list/search result)

format.description: Format constraint for scalar string parameters, e.g. hex_color.

pattern.description: Regex source for scalar string parameters.

item_format.description: Format constraint for string_array items, e.g. hex_color.

item_format.description: Format constraint for string_array items, e.g. hex_color.

purpose.description: Set on shortlisted models: what this model is the default choice for.

unlim.description: Whether the caller can spend free-trial unlimited generations right now. Combine with a model's supports_unlim before passing use_unlim:true to generate_image / generate_video / generate_audio.

available.description: True when the caller can spend free-trial unlimited generations right now.

remaining.description: Remaining unlimited generations; null means unmetered.

expires_at.description: ISO timestamp when the allowance lapses.

related_tools.description: Standalone tools (not catalog models) relevant to the search query — e.g. motion_control for recast/puppeteer, upscale_image/upscale_video for enhance, outpaint_image for expand/uncrop, reframe for a video aspect-ratio change, remove_background for cutout. Call the named tool directly; it will not appear in items.

tools.name: generate_image
tools.title: Generate Image
tools.description: Generate one image request and render its result(s) in the generation widget. Use count 2-4 only for variants of the same prompt, inputs, and settings; for 2-12 independent image requests with different prompts or inputs, use the headless generate_image_batch tool instead. Attached/local media: if your code environment can read the file, upload it yourself (`media_upload`, curl PUT, `media_confirm`); otherwise call `media_upload_widget`. Do not ask for Claude chat attachments because remote tools cannot read them. Web media URL: call `media_import_url`, then pass returned `media_id`; `medias[].value` must be media_id/job_id, not URL. With no model named by the user, pick it from the shortlist: `models_explore` with action `list` and type `image`. Use the first model of that type unless another entry's `purpose` fits the request, and keep the model for follow-ups in the same series. `gpt_image_2_6` and `gpt_image_2_6_flare` support native animated GIF and SVG output: use one of them for a GIF or SVG request and set `output_format` to `gif` or `svg` among the model-specific params. For a GIF request use this image tool directly, not video generation or conversion. GIF accepts references and live size/frame_count/frame_duration_ms controls; SVG is generation-only without references. Preserve explicit model choices. Monsters, creatures, aliens, hybrids or 'turn me into a monster': first load `get_preset_instructions` with `{ preset: "/monsters" }`. Ambiguous create-character/avatar: offer reusable Soul training (5-20 photos, ~10 min) vs one-off; do not train generic silently. For interactive Soul training, open `soul_train_wizard` before uploading photos. In headless clients, call `show_characters(action='train')` only after explicit user approval. Use `models_explore` for aspect_ratios, params, medias roles. Top-level model params; apply `adjustments`. If `recovery_tool` returned, call it immediately; do not explain/ask first. Price a request with `estimate_image_cost`; `get_cost` is not accepted here. `use_unlim` selects allowance (true) or credits (false). Omit it to follow an existing choice or receive `unlim_choice` when an eligible allowance needs a decision; that response submits no job. Ask the user and repeat the request with their explicit choice. On a transport timeout the submission outcome may be unknown: do not automatically resubmit. Reuse returned job IDs and retry only after the original outcome is known. A prompt already in a sandbox file or a slash command's text block can be passed as `params.prompt: {"ref": "sandbox:<path>#<pointer>"}` or `{"ref": "preset:/<command>"}` instead of being typed again. After a quote, `params: {"ref": "<its quote_ref>"}` generates exactly the quoted params without typing them again.

model.description: Model ID from the model catalog (required).

prompt.description: Text description of what to generate. Or `{ "ref": "sandbox:<path>#<pointer>" }` / `{ "ref": "preset:/<command>" }` when the text is already in a sandbox file or a slash command's text block, so it is not typed again.

ref.description: `sandbox:<path>` for a whole UTF-8 file under /home/user in the Higgsfield sandbox, or `sandbox:<path>#<JSON Pointer>` for one value of a JSON file, e.g. `sandbox:~/film/plan.json#/clips/3/prompt`; `preset:/<command>` for the fenced ```text block of a slash command from get_preset_instructions (`#<n>` picks the n-th when it has several); `quote:<id>` for the params of a cost quote, as its `quote_ref` gave them.

count.description: Number of variants (1-4) generated from this same prompt, inputs, and settings and rendered together in one widget. Use the matching generate_*_batch tool for independent prompts or inputs. Ignored with use_unlim: an unlim request is always one generation — count is capped to 1 and the cap comes back in adjustments.

folder_id.description: Destination folder for this conversation. Use default_folder_id from create_project, or folder_id from create_folder when requested. Reuse on every generation and batch item in this conversation; never invent an ID or share a destination across chats. Omit by default for generation without a project. Before the first generation without a destination, call get_preferences: create a project only when auto_create_project is true or explicitly requested. Explicit existing destinations and requests to work without a project take priority; never change the saved preference for a one-off request.

use_free_gens.description: Request free generation only when the user explicitly asks. For a Katana run, also pass preset_session_id from get_katana_config; the backend validates eligibility. Do not combine with use_unlim or retry a rejected free request on credits without explicit approval. true caps count to 1.

preset_session_id.description: Session returned by get_katana_config for every Katana preset run, paid or free. Forward this ID on every generation and batch item in that run, including cost estimates. Add use_free_gens: true only when the user explicitly requests free generations; otherwise omit it.

run_id.description: The run id from the Run id section of the instructions of a command that issues one (/short-drama, /shorts): the same on every generation, batch item and cost estimate of that run. It only ties the run's jobs together. Omit it when the instructions have no Run id section; never put it in preset_session_id.

drama_ads_id.description: The drama_ads_id get_drama_ads_config returned, when this generation belongs to that drama: repeat it on every generation and batch item of the drama. Never sent to the model.

value.description: UUID from media_upload/media_import_url or job_id from a prior generation. Do not pass https:// URLs here.

role.description: Role — varies by model; inspect the selected model's medias[].roles. Server may auto-coerce when unambiguous.

use_unlim.description: Which balance pays for this generation: the caller's free-trial unlimited generations (true) or their credits (false). OMIT IT to let the server decide — if they hold an allowance that covers the model, the tool submits nothing and returns `unlim_choice`, the question to put to the user before spending anything of theirs. Answer it by calling again with the same params plus this field; the answer is remembered for a few minutes, so a multi-step flow is asked once. true also caps count to 1. Whichever way it is set, a rejected opt-in is reported rather than quietly replaced with a charge.

ref.description: `sandbox:<path>` for a whole UTF-8 file under /home/user in the Higgsfield sandbox, or `sandbox:<path>#<JSON Pointer>` for one value of a JSON file, e.g. `sandbox:~/film/plan.json#/clips/3/prompt`; `preset:/<command>` for the fenced ```text block of a slash command from get_preset_instructions (`#<n>` picks the n-th when it has several); `quote:<id>` for the params of a cost quote, as its `quote_ref` gave them.

anyOf.description: A reference naming the params, e.g. the `quote_ref` of a cost quote. Any other key sent next to `ref` replaces the named params' own.

context.description: Briefly describe the user's underlying goal and why this call helps, in one short sentence. Do not include names, contact details, credentials, URLs, or biometric details. Analytics only; not a generation prompt.

input_check.description: Genjutsu required-media presence only. A successful price quote does not validate media existence, duration or generation readiness.

prepared_params.description: Genjutsu request params with resolved media UUIDs and applied adjustments. May be incomplete; inspect input_check. Reuse instead of importing the same references again. No generation has been submitted or validated.

exrUrl.description: Original EXR ZIP; when present, rawUrl is the unprocessed input video used for playback.

tools.name: generate_video
tools.title: Generate Video
tools.description: Generate one direct video request and render it in the generation widget. Use count 2-4 only for variants of the same prompt, inputs, and settings; use headless generate_video_batch for 2-12 independent requests. GENJUTSU TRIGGERS: route `Higgsfield Genjutsu` by intent. Copy, repeat, reproduce, mimic, or transfer motion, movement, actions, gestures, dance, or camera motion from one driving video to reference-image subjects -> `hf_mult_motion_control`. Replace, change, or swap an object, product, garment, or character in one source video from reference images -> `hf_mult_replace_object`. These are direct `generate_video` models, not legacy `motion_control` or `ad-multiplier`; reserve ad-multiplier for explicitly requested independent variants. Pass images with role `image` and exactly one source/driving video with role `video`. LOCAL/ATTACHED INPUT GATE: without confirmed media_id values, upload readable files yourself first (`media_upload`, curl PUT, `media_confirm`); only if unreadable or the PUT fails, call `media_upload_widget` as the only tool in that turn. Never ask for a chat attachment. For mixed image+video use type:`auto`, multiple:true. For web media call `media_import_url`; `medias[].value` must be media_id/job_id. With no model named by the user, pick it from the shortlist: `models_explore` with action `list` and type `video`. Use the first model of that type unless another entry's `purpose` fits the request, and keep the model for follow-ups in the same series. For guided product/ad creation, open `show_marketing_studio_v2`. For an explicitly requested direct `marketing_studio_video` call, inspect its current model schema and use only confirmed supported IDs and parameters. Use declared media roles and model-supported audio only. Use models_explore for durations/params. For `sync_so` lipsync of dialogue or several faces (wrong face moves), pass `segments`: one per speaker turn from the transcript, each with start_time/end_time (omit audio_start_time/audio_end_time to reuse that segment window), and its own `active_speaker_detection` (frame_number+coordinates of that speaker); one speaker needs no segments. Apply adjustments and immediately call any recovery_tool. Price a request with estimate_video_cost; get_cost is not accepted here. Set use_unlim:true only when explicitly requested. On a transport timeout the submission outcome may be unknown: do not automatically resubmit. Reuse returned job IDs and retry only after the original outcome is known. A prompt already in a sandbox file or a slash command's text block can be passed as `params.prompt: {"ref": "sandbox:<path>#<pointer>"}` or `{"ref": "preset:/<command>"}` instead of being typed again. After a quote, `params: {"ref": "<its quote_ref>"}` generates exactly the quoted params without typing them again.

model.description: Model ID from the model catalog (required).

prompt.description: Text description of what to generate. Optional for Marketing Studio workflows. Or `{ "ref": "sandbox:<path>#<pointer>" }` / `{ "ref": "preset:/<command>" }` when the text is already in a sandbox file or a slash command's text block, so it is not typed again.

ref.description: `sandbox:<path>` for a whole UTF-8 file under /home/user in the Higgsfield sandbox, or `sandbox:<path>#<JSON Pointer>` for one value of a JSON file, e.g. `sandbox:~/film/plan.json#/clips/3/prompt`; `preset:/<command>` for the fenced ```text block of a slash command from get_preset_instructions (`#<n>` picks the n-th when it has several); `quote:<id>` for the params of a cost quote, as its `quote_ref` gave them.

Use the matching generate_*_batch tool for independent prompts or inputs. Ignored with use_unlim: an unlim request is always one generation — count is capped to 1 and the cap comes back in adjustments.

aspect_ratio.description: Output aspect ratio. Use '9:16' for vertical/portrait platforms (TikTok, Reels, YouTube Shorts) and '16:9' for horizontal/landscape. When omitted the model default applies, which is landscape ('16:9') for Marketing Studio — so pass '9:16' explicitly for TikTok/Reels output. Alternatively pass explicit width/height (e.g. width:1080,height:1920) and the backend derives the aspect ratio.

folder_id.description: Destination folder for this conversation. Use default_folder_id from create_project, or folder_id from create_folder when requested. Reuse on every generation and batch item in this conversation; never invent an ID or share a destination across chats. Omit by default for generation without a project. Before the first generation without a destination, call get_preferences: create a project only when auto_create_project is true or explicitly requested. Explicit existing destinations and requests to work without a project take priority; never change the saved preference for a one-off request.

tools.description: Generate one music or speech/voice request and render it in the generation widget. A prompt already in a sandbox file or a slash command's text block can be passed as `params.prompt: {"ref": "sandbox:<path>#<pointer>"}` or `{"ref": "preset:/<command>"}` instead of being typed again. A quote returns `quote_ref`; generate exactly the quoted request with `params: {"ref": "<quote_ref>"}` instead of typing the params again.

tools.description: Generate a 3D GLB mesh. For a model from a photo, first load `get_preset_instructions` with `{ preset: "/photo-to-3d-model" }`: it picks the model, texturing and polygon budget. In a Blender scene (Blender Studio or local Blender) build with Python by default: a request to build, model or recreate something in Blender, even from an attached picture, means modelling it in Blender. Do not call this tool there, not even with get_cost:true, unless the user asks for image-to-3D or a generated mesh by name or approves it after it was offered; never wrap the source picture around a mesh as its texture. Hosted 3D Jutsu cannot import the result. Use `models_explore(type:'3d')` to pick a model and see its `medias[].roles` and `parameters`. Attached/local file: upload it yourself if readable (`media_upload`, curl PUT, `media_confirm`), else call `media_upload_widget`; remote tools cannot read Claude chat attachments. Web media URL: call `media_import_url`, pass returned `media_id`; `medias[].value` must be media_id/job_id, not URL. Defaults: `image_to_3d` for general image-to-3D with optional texturing, PBR, and rigging (pass `should_texture:true` unless bare geometry is wanted); `multi_image_to_3d` when 2-4 views of the same subject are available (better geometric accuracy); `sam_3_3d` for single-object reconstruction; `3d_rigging` to rig an existing 3D model (takes `model_url`, not images — pass the completed model's public HTTPS GLB URL, not a job ID; for a GLB made in the sandbox, upload it with `media_upload` (a .glb filename), curl PUT and `media_confirm` type file, then pass the `url` media_upload returned, never its `upload_url`). For animated rigs, search clip ids with the `animation_actions` tool and pass `animation_action_id` with `enable_animation:true`. For image-to-3D, the mesh reproduces what is in the source image — to add or change props, clothing, or held objects, edit the image first with `generate_image`, then convert the edited result. For text-to-3D, discover the current model and inspect its prompt requirements before submitting. Put all generation arguments inside `params`, with model-specific fields beside `model`. Apply `adjustments` returned by the server. If `recovery_tool` is returned, call it immediately. `get_cost:true` preflights credits without submitting. tools.name: get_presets
tools.title: Browse Media Presets
tools.description: Search and browse reusable image and video generation presets from Higgsfield's Viral, Marketing Studio, Genjutsu, Katana, Soul and personal Recraft style galleries, or retrieve a preset's inputs and preview without starting a generation. For sources other than Katana, Soul, Recraft and Faceless Channel: A bare preset slash command or a request to open, preview, or browse a preset only opens its widget. For supplied attachments, use input_schema from get_preset_instructions to map and upload the relevant files before opening any widget. Call get_presets exactly once with source, preset_id and initial_inputs in the exact schema fields. Do not call get_presets just to inspect the schema. Leave omitted settings to schema defaults; never reopen the detail merely to repeat default selections. Never assume one photo satisfies all requirements or guess ambiguous slot assignments. Leave missing fields in the prefilled widget for the user. Stop after opening the detail and let the user interact with it. Do not call execute_preset unless the user explicitly asks to generate, or submits with Recreate in the widget. Check execution.readiness for the supplied inputs before execution; collect missing or invalid fields instead of submitting. execution.available indicates capability, not permission; optional inputs and built-in media do not authorize generation. Readiness checks input structure, not media ownership or upload confirmation; use only confirmed media IDs. If the widget reports submitted job IDs, display and wait for those jobs without executing again. Where supported, pass query to search preset names, descriptions and types before pagination. All query words must match; omit source to search Viral and Marketing Studio. Pass preset_id to open a published preset detail preview directly. Omit source to browse Viral and Marketing Studio; limit applies to the complete page. source='genjutsu' lists Genjutsu motion presets, with category='genjutsu', 'genjutsu-trending' or 'genjutsu-new'; a bare /genjutsu opens this gallery. To choose motion for an existing AI Influencer, pass initial_inputs:{character_sheet:[{id:"<confirmed sheet job UUID>",type:"image_job"}]} — character_sheet must be a one-item array, not a single object; legacy source='marketing_studio' still accepts these categories and genjutsu: IDs. category='genjutsu-styles' lists Genjutsu Styles: named looks (e.g. Knitted Yarn World, Rounded Toy CGI) that redraw the user's own video while keeping its motion. When the user names a look, search it with query; preset_id 'genjutsu-style:<id>' opens its form, and initial_inputs {video:[<confirmed video UUID>], references?, resolution} adds readiness and price. source='soul' browses Soul 2.0 image styles: the user's own custom presets (moodboards, including ones added from a share link) first, then the curated catalog. Search with query or open a style with preset_id and source='soul'. Each item's id is the style_id for generate_image or generate_image_batch with model='soul_2'; do not call execute_preset for Soul styles. A style can be combined with soul_id, but not with medias/image references. Preview images are catalog samples, not generation inputs. Browsing or selecting a style does not authorize generation. source='recraft' browses the caller's own completed Recraft styles saved in Higgsfield, not general presets or styles in a separate Recraft account. Search names by substring with query or open a style with its UUID as preset_id. Each item's id is the style_id for generate_image or generate_image_batch with model='recraft_v4_styles', not recraft_v4_1. Do not call execute_preset for these styles. Preview images are samples, not generation inputs. Browsing or selecting a style does not authorize generation. An empty catalog means no matching ready personal styles are available; do not substitute a general style. source='viral' lists Viral Hub chain presets for /effects requests; source='marketing_studio' lists Marketing Studio templates: for /product use category='product-shot', for /motion use category='motion'. source='katana' is a user-facing catalog, not headless search: query and initial_inputs are unsupported. preset_id:'<slug>' opens one Katana preset's input form directly; use it only as the loaded /katana/slug instructions direct, when the user asked to run that preset and its inputs are missing. To find or choose a Katana preset for a task, call get_preset_instructions with preset omitted, match the returned titles/descriptions, then load its exact /katana/slug. Do not open this gallery merely to choose a preset for supplied media. Explicit catalog browsing opens the Katana catalog without default filters; category supports personalized_edits, style_transfer and motion_transfer, katana_source supports community or higgsfield. Katana uses opaque string cursors and backend-default page sizes (explicit limit maximum 20). Recreate selections resolve exact /katana/slug instructions with get_preset_instructions. Katana browsing does not execute a preset. source='what_if' opens the What If style gallery of /content-factory, where the user picks a style and types the prompt; call it only for a bare /content-factory or when the user asks to browse What If styles, never when a topic is given. It takes no other filters and does not start a generation. source='shorts_studio' opens the Shorts Studio preset gallery of /shorts, where the user picks a style and types the topic or script; call it only for a bare /shorts or when the user asks to browse Shorts Studio presets. It takes no other filters and does not start a generation. source='faceless_channel' opens the Faceless Video style picker without filters. Use the selected preset ID with the Faceless Video style resolver. source='music_cards' opens the Musical Cards gallery of /musical-cards: example cards to start from and a step-by-step form (the occasion, who it is for and from, the look); call it only for a bare /musical-cards or when the user asks to browse musical card templates, or with preset_id when a message from the website names a Musical Cards template and its INPUTS carry preset_id and no name: preset_id, the template's id from that message, opens the same gallery on that template's form. With either call pass music_card when you already know who the card is for, so the form opens filled in. It takes no other filters (the widget loads its own shelves) and does not start a generation. source='short_drama' opens the look gallery of /short-drama, where the user picks the series' visual style; call it only as the loaded /short-drama instructions direct. Optional preset_id is the style id you recommend for this script: it is shown first, marked Recommended. It takes no other filters and does not start a generation. Use category slugs returned by this tool and pass next_cursor only when the user asks for another page.

initial_inputs.description: Prefill a selected preset using execution.input_schema. Use confirmed media UUIDs in the correct slots, never local paths. Partial inputs are allowed; inspect execution.readiness. Requires preset_id, except category=genjutsu, genjutsu-trending or genjutsu-new accepts character_sheet to prefill the motion gallery. For Genjutsu use character_sheet:[{id:<confirmed UUID>,type:image_job}] for an existing character sheet, or type:media_input for an uploaded image. The field is always a one-item array, never a single object. Does not submit.

source.description: Gallery source. Omit for the combined feed.

katana_source.description: Katana catalog filter. Only valid with source=katana.

preset_id.description: For source=recraft, the UUID of your saved style; search names with query. Otherwise, published preset ID (or its catalog slug / exact name) to open directly in the detail preview. Source is optional if the ID is unique. Use category='all' and omit cursor (or pass 0) for a detail lookup.

category.description: Category slug. Optional for Katana, which defaults to the Community source; defaults to 'all' for other galleries. Other categories require source.

query.description: Not supported for source=katana; use get_preset_instructions with preset omitted for Katana discovery. For source=recraft, search personal style names by case-insensitive substring (maximum 80 characters). Other sources search original CMS names, descriptions and preset types; words may match different fields. Empty means browse. Cannot be combined with preset_id.

cursor.description: Pass next_cursor with the same filters. Katana uses an opaque string cursor; other galleries use numeric offsets. Omit when changing filters.

limit.description: Number of presets across the complete page, 1–50. Defaults to 12; Katana defaults to 4 and allows 1–20.

music_card.description: Only with source='music_cards': what you already know about the person the card is for, from this conversation and your memory of the user, so the form opens filled in and the user only checks it. Never ask the user for it first; omit it when you know nothing or cannot tell who the card is for (a template's title and occasion say who: "I love you, Mom" is for the user's mother). Only what suits a greeting sung aloud to that person: never health, money, conflicts or secrets, nothing sad or private; in doubt, leave it out. Nothing is generated from it: the user sees it in the form, changes it and presses Generate.

name.description: The person's name as the user says it.

role.description: Who they are to the user, in a word or two: Mom, best friend, boss.

facts.description: At most three facts or wishes, one short line each (aim for under 40 characters), as you know them and nothing made up; each is sung as written.

occasion.description: Without preset_id only: the occasion in a word or two (Birthday, New Year).

tools.name: execute_preset
tools.title: Execute Preset
tools.description: Request execution of one published preset from the Viral, Marketing Studio or Genjutsu gallery, including a Genjutsu Style (genjutsu-style: preset_id) that restyles the user's own video. A bare preset slash command or a request to open, preview, or browse a preset only opens its widget. For supplied attachments, use input_schema from get_preset_instructions to map and upload the relevant files before opening any widget. Call get_presets exactly once with source, preset_id and initial_inputs in the exact schema fields. Do not call get_presets just to inspect the schema. Leave omitted settings to schema defaults; never reopen the detail merely to repeat default selections. Never assume one photo satisfies all requirements or guess ambiguous slot assignments. Leave missing fields in the prefilled widget for the user. Stop after opening the detail and let the user interact with it. Do not call execute_preset unless the user explicitly asks to generate, or submits with Recreate in the widget. Check execution.readiness for the supplied inputs before execution; collect missing or invalid fields instead of submitting. execution.available indicates capability, not permission; optional inputs and built-in media do not authorize generation. Readiness checks input structure, not media ownership or upload confirmation; use only confirmed media IDs. If the widget reports submitted job IDs, display and wait for those jobs without executing again. Check execution.available in the preset detail before calling. Unavailable execution returns an error without submitting a job. Use get_presets to obtain the published preset_id and source; do not invent either value. A successful submission returns final job_ids; a preset may produce multiple outputs. Use job_display for one job, jobs_wait and show_generation_by_ids for multiple jobs. Preset-specific inputs are a free-form object; their requirements are defined by the selected preset, not by this tool schema.

source.description: Published gallery source. Genjutsu also accepts legacy marketing_studio.

preset_id.description: Published preset ID returned by get_presets; its catalog slug or exact name is also accepted.

inputs.description: Free-form inputs for the selected preset; use its execution.input_schema when available.

job_ids.description: Final output jobs from the preset workflow; may contain multiple IDs. Intermediate workflow steps are not outputs.

tools.name: reveal_generation
tools.title: Reveal IP-Detected Generation
tools.description: Confirm the user has rights to the content of an `ip_detected` generation and flip its status to `completed`. Backend accepts only seedance-family jobs (cs_3_0, seedance_2_0, ms_video, etc) and only while the job is still in `ip_detected` state. Returns the updated generation. Used by the job-list widget's Reveal button after the user accepts the rights confirmation modal.

jobId.description: Job ID of the `ip_detected` generation to reveal.

exrUrl.description: Original EXR ZIP; when present, rawUrl is the unprocessed input video used for playback.

request_id.description: MCP server HTTP request ID for support/debugging. If present, show it to the user.

tools.name: track_generation_download
tools.title: Track Generation Download
tools.description: Record a generation download started by the authenticated user in the app.

tools.name: set_generation_like
tools.title: Set Generation Like
tools.description: Like or unlike a generation for the authenticated user from the app. Sets the requested state; repeated requests are safe. Pass folder_id when acting from a project so its LIKE permission is checked; unlike removes only the user's own bookmark even after access is revoked.

tools.name: prepare_generation
tools.title: Prepare Generation Settings
tools.description: Read a source generation's original model and complete parameters for the app's Recreate context. Prepares settings for the next user request; does not submit or generate anything.

tools.name: jobs_wait
tools.title: Wait For Generation Jobs
tools.description: Long-poll 1-12 generation jobs together without opening a widget. Waits up to timeout_seconds (default 15, max 15) for every job to reach a terminal state, then returns compact indexed statuses and result URLs. Use job IDs returned by generate_image_batch, generate_video_batch, or generate_audio_batch. For larger sets, choose groups of at most 12 and wait for each group. Permanent lookup failures are returned once without blocking the other jobs; transient lookup failures are retried within the timeout. A failed, nsfw or ip_detected job may carry error: the reason in words to tell the user. When all_terminal is false, wait poll_after_seconds before calling again. After every wait group in the user's generation set is terminal, collect their indexed jobs and display them with one show_generation_by_ids call when within that tool's limit. Never use show_generations or call job_display once per batch job.

index.description: Stable index returned by the batch generation tool.

jobs.description: Full-profile generation jobs to wait for together.

timeout_seconds.description: Long-poll budget. Use 0 for an immediate snapshot.

exr_url.description: Original EXR ZIP; result_url is the unchanged input video, not processed HDR.

retryable.description: Present for lookup_failed. True means a later jobs_wait call may succeed; false means the lookup failure is permanent.

all_terminal.description: True when every job is terminal or permanently unresolvable, so no further polling is needed.

tools.name: show_generation_by_ids
tools.title: Show Generations By IDs
tools.description: Render exactly 1-60 requested generation jobs in the full-profile gallery widget, ordered by index and paginated locally in groups of 12. Use once every jobs_wait group is terminal for generate_image_batch, generate_video_batch, or generate_audio_batch. Pass the complete indexed set collected from the batch tools. This tool fetches only those job IDs in bounded groups: it never loads generation history, uses cursors, requests additional pages, or adds other jobs. Do not use show_generations or job_display to present a completed batch.

index.description: Stable index returned by the batch generation tool.

tools.name: media_upload
tools.title: Upload Media
tools.description: Upload media for use in generation, or general files (documents, archives, code) for sharing. Returns presigned URLs for clients that can upload bytes themselves; run the generated curl commands or PUT the bytes to each upload_url, then call media_confirm. The media type is inferred from the filename extension: image/video/audio extensions become generation inputs; other whitelisted extensions (pdf, zip, tar, docx, csv, code files, …) are uploaded as general files and return a permanent URL, but cannot be used as generation inputs. General files are the agent's own upload path — the widget does not accept them, so upload the bytes to upload_url yourself (e.g. from a code execution environment). Supports batch uploads via files[]. Default path for user-attached image/video/audio whose bytes your code environment can read (e.g. /mnt/user-data/uploads in Claude): call this, PUT the file to upload_url with curl, then media_confirm — do not ask the user to re-upload. Fall back to media_upload_widget only when the file is unreadable or the PUT fails.

tools.title: Upload Local Media
tools.description: Fallback local-media intake for Higgsfield in Apps UI-capable clients. tools.name: scene_builder_3d_create_project
tools.title: 3D Jutsu: create project
tools.description:
Create a new private 3D Jutsu project for the authenticated user. Supply a descriptive name; the service assigns ownership and the project ID. Use this when the user requests a new project or a new standalone scene. A hosted scene is free to build: nothing to rent, and building, editing and rendering spend no credits (only an AI image or video from a render does). Blender Studio is the paid prosumer alternative: full Blender on a rented GPU box, billed in credits by the second. For an existing scene, use scene_builder_3d_list_projects instead. Pass the returned projectId explicitly to subsequent tools; creation does not set a global active project. Call scene_builder_3d_get_project, then scene_builder_3d_query_python to inspect the initial scene and obtain guards before scene_builder_3d_run_python or scene_builder_3d_import_asset. Creation alone does not produce a committed GLB: scene_builder_3d_show_scene becomes available after the first successful edit or import. This call is not idempotent. If the response is interrupted or uncertain, use scene_builder_3d_list_projects to find the new project before retrying; repeating creation can create a duplicate.

Before building or editing a scene, load get_preset_instructions with { preset: "/3d-jutsu" } once for the full workflow, runtime limits and scene-building references.

tools.name: scene_builder_3d_query_python
tools.title: 3D Jutsu: query python
tools.description:
Inspect the latest settled Blender scene without committing changes. `bpy` and the `artifacts`
registry are available; assign concise JSON-serializable findings to `result`. Query exact
names, metre-scale dimensions, transforms, parents, collections, materials, cameras, lights,
visibility, and animation settings as needed. Inspect Blender RNA when an API or enum is
uncertain. Temporary scene changes are discarded, including camera changes used for inspection.
A query can render and publish images for visual inspection: allocate a target with
`artifacts.file(name="preview.png", media_type="image/png")`, write the image to `target.path`,
and call `target.publish()`. Resolve published IDs with `scene_builder_3d_get_artifact`.
Use the successful query's `revisionBefore` and `sceneSequenceAfter` as the guards for the next
`scene_builder_3d_run_python` call. If still active, poll `scene_builder_3d_get_operation`.
Reuse an operation ID only to retry the identical request. Imported model bytes must enter
through `scene_builder_3d_import_asset`; do not fetch URLs or embed file bytes in Python.

code.description: Use bpy and artifacts; assign JSON-serializable findings to result. Files persist only via artifacts.file(name=..., media_type=...), writing to target.path, then target.publish(). At most eight PNG/JPEG/MP4 files, 512 MiB each and 1 GiB total; images at most 16384 pixels per side and 64 MP. Invalid published files fail the operation. Set image_settings.media_type='IMAGE' before PNG/JPEG, or 'VIDEO' before FFMPEG with MPEG4/H264. No network fetches or embedded model bytes; use scene_builder_3d_import_asset.

tools.name: scene_builder_3d_run_python
tools.title: 3D Jutsu: run python
tools.description:
Commit one coherent Blender scene edit against the exact revision and scene sequence you
inspected with `scene_builder_3d_get_project` or `scene_builder_3d_query_python`. `bpy` and
`artifacts` are available; assign JSON-serializable findings to `result`. Keep one mutation
active per project, including imports. If this operation remains active, poll
`scene_builder_3d_get_operation` before editing again. Reuse `operationId` only for the identical
code and preconditions. On a stale-state conflict, inspect the scene again and regenerate the
edit with fresh guards and a new operation ID. REVISION_CONFLICT rejects the submission: do not poll that operation ID. A successful mutation advances `revisionAfter`.

This worker pins Blender 5.2: use `BLENDER_EEVEE`, `BLENDER_WORKBENCH`, or `CYCLES`, not
`BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT`. Code is capped at 256 KiB, and execution and checkpoint/export must fit
the configured worker deadline; keep renders small and split expensive work into coherent edits.
Do not invent texture paths or fetch external files from Blender; use
`scene_builder_3d_import_asset` for models.

Successful execution does not establish visual correctness. Render from the delivery camera,
publish the image through `artifacts`, retrieve it with `scene_builder_3d_get_artifact`, and
inspect it before claiming completion. If visual inspection is unavailable, state what remains
unverified. Use `scene_builder_3d_get_glb` or `scene_builder_3d_get_blend` when the user needs
the committed files.

Before building or editing a scene, load get_preset_instructions with { preset: "/3d-jutsu" } once for the full workflow, runtime limits and scene-building references.

Finish each completed scene creation, edit, or import task by calling `scene_builder_3d_show_scene` once as the final scene inspection/edit call of that review phase, after mutations have settled and verification is complete. Pass the same `projectId` and the exact committed `revision` of the final result: `revisionAfter` from the final successful mutation, or the settled `project.revision` after an import. Do not guess the revision. Show an unchanged revision only once. Authorized generation and status calls may follow; later feedback or a verified mismatch can reopen scene editing. Verify and show the corrected revision at its next review boundary. This shows the result to the user; a text summary or download link alone does not finish scene delivery.

revision and scene sequence for subsequent work; obtain published images and videos through

deciding to retry. Do not blindly resubmit a failed operation under another ID.

import, inspect dimensions, placement, orientation, contact, and materials with
`scene_builder_3d_query_python` before further edits. Do not repeat the whole import to poll:
it can create a duplicate. If an import fails, report the error; never fall back to Python
network calls or base64-encoded model bytes. Copy catalogSearch from the search result's importArguments. If settled is false, poll scene_builder_3d_get_project until appliedSceneSequence reaches targetSceneSequence. If submissionUnknown is true, inspect the returned entityId before deciding to retry. tools.title: 3D Jutsu: get glb
tools.description:
For an interactive scene preview use `scene_builder_3d_show_scene`. Resolve a short-lived download for the current committed GLB, or a specified historical
revision. This retrieves an existing export; it does not run Blender, render, or create a new
export. Settle any active mutation with `scene_builder_3d_get_operation` first if you need its
result. Use GLB for portable scene delivery, and `scene_builder_3d_get_blend` for the editable
Blender source. Procedural shading, world lighting, and some Blender features may differ in
GLB. A successful download does not establish that the exported scene looks correct.

projectId.description: Project ID from scene_builder_3d_list_projects, scene_builder_3d_create_project, or the user's explicit selection. Required on every project-scoped tool.

revision.description: Exact committed revision inspected; do not guess.

tools.name: scene_builder_3d_get_blend
tools.title: 3D Jutsu: get blend
tools.description:
Resolve a short-lived download for the current committed editable Blender file, or a specified
historical revision. This retrieves the existing scene; it does not create a revision or
render a preview. Settle any active mutation with `scene_builder_3d_get_operation` first when
you need its result. Use `scene_builder_3d_get_glb` for portable model delivery and
`scene_builder_3d_get_artifact` for published images or videos.

projectId.description: Project ID from scene_builder_3d_list_projects, scene_builder_3d_create_project, or the user's explicit selection. Required on every project-scoped tool.

revision.description: Exact committed revision inspected; do not guess.

tools.name: scene_builder_3d_get_artifact
tools.title: 3D Jutsu: get artifact
tools.description:
Resolve a short-lived download for an image or video that a successful Python operation
published through `artifacts`. Use the artifact ID and operation ID or revision returned by
that operation; do not invent IDs or filesystem paths. Query artifacts can be operation-scoped
without a new committed revision. This retrieves an existing artifact and does not render one.
To create a preview, render and publish it with `scene_builder_3d_query_python` or
`scene_builder_3d_run_python`. Inspect the returned image using the client's image capability
before judging framing, lighting, materials, and geometry. If the client cannot inspect it,
describe that limitation rather than claiming a visual check passed.

tools.name: video_analysis_create
tools.title: Create Video Analysis
tools.description: Start a scene-by-scene analysis of a video. Provide EXACTLY ONE of: (a) video_input_id — UUID of a video the user has uploaded via media_upload/media_confirm, or (b) youtube_url — a YouTube link (youtube.com / youtu.be hosts only). Optionally pass prompt to ask a question about the video instead (answered in result.analysis), and mode='glance' for a faster, cheaper pass. Each analysis costs credits; if the user lacks them, the call fails with an upgrade link. Returns immediately with status='queued'; poll video_analysis_status until status='completed'. Processing typically takes 3-5 minutes on average. IMPORTANT: warn the user up front that the longer the video, the less accurate the scene-by-scene analysis becomes — short clips give the most reliable results.

video_input_id.description: UUID of the uploaded source video (the media_id returned by the upload tool).

youtube_url.description: HTTPS YouTube video URL on youtube.com, www.youtube.com, m.youtube.com, or youtu.be.

prompt.description: Optional question about the video (e.g. "what product is shown?"). The answer comes back as text in result.analysis instead of the scene-by-scene storyboard in result.scenes. Omit for the storyboard.

mode.description: Analysis depth: "deep" (default) is the richer analysis; "glance" is a fast, cheaper triage.

tools.title: Video Analysis Status
tools.description: Get the status and result of a video analysis. Poll this after video_analysis_create until status='completed' (scenes populated, or analysis when a prompt was asked) or 'failed' (fail_reason populated). Analyses typically finish in 3-5 minutes — poll accordingly every 30-60 seconds.

tools.description: Expand or reframe an existing video to a new aspect ratio while preserving the source content. Use this when the user asks to make a video vertical, horizontal, square, wider, taller, or fill new edges around a video. role.description: Use image for references that guide filled edges. Use start_image only when the user provides a first-frame anchor.

tools.name: create_voice
tools.title: Create Voice
tools.description: Open the Create Voice Apps UI. Call this immediately when the user asks to create a voice, call the Create Voice tool, or needs a local browser record/upload surface and no confirmed audio_media_id is already present. Do not ask the user to upload an audio file or provide the name in chat first; the widget collects the required name plus record/upload audio. If the user already has or attached an audio file in chat, still call this tool with initial_tab='upload' — remote tools cannot read Claude chat attachments, so the user re-selects the file in the widget's Upload tab (it uploads directly to Higgsfield). Do not try to pass a chat attachment or ask for a URL. The widget records/uploads, confirms the audio, and creates the voice itself end-to-end — and if the user is out of credits or on a free plan it shows the plans/credits UI inline. After the widget reports success you do NOT need to call create_voice_from_confirmed_audio again. Only call create_voice_from_confirmed_audio yourself when a confirmed audio_media_id is already present in the prompt and no UI step is needed.

name.description: Initial name to prefill in the UI.

initial_tab.description: Initial tab for the create voice UI. Defaults to record. Use 'upload' when the user already has or attached an audio file.

mode.description: Discriminator for the widget's initial view.

initial_tab.description: Initial tab for the create voice UI.

resource_uri.description: URI of the UI resource this tool binds to.

microphone_required.description: True when the record tab may request browser microphone permission.

name.description: Initial name to prefill in the UI.

tools.name: create_voice_from_confirmed_audio
tools.title: Create Voice From Confirmed Audio
tools.description: Backend-only creation of a cloned voice from an already confirmed audio upload. Do not call this tool until audio_media_id and name are already known. For direct creation, first upload speech audio with media_upload, PUT the bytes, then call media_confirm with type='audio'. Pass that confirmed media_id here as audio_media_id plus a required name. If the user needs to record or upload local audio in an Apps UI-capable client, call create_voice instead; that widget records/uploads, confirms, and creates the voice itself, so you do not call this tool for the UI flow. The audio should be clear speech, roughly 10 seconds to 3 minutes, and no larger than the upload limit. The backend charges the voice-clone credit cost on successful creation. Cloning is asynchronous: on success the tool returns the new voice_id plus a status, and a fresh clone is usually still 'processing' and not yet usable. Use the returned voice_id with voice_type='element' for generate_audio or voice_change only once it is ready (status='completed' and is_audio_eligible=true). If status is 'processing' or is_audio_eligible is not true, the clone is still training — re-check it with list_voices before generating instead of submitting right away; status 'voice_clone_failed'/'failed' means cloning did not succeed. If recovery_tool is returned, call it immediately; do not explain/ask first.

name.description: Required display name for the created voice.

description.description: Optional voice description for backend metadata.

voice.description: Created voice. Use voice_id with voice_type='element' once status='completed' and is_audio_eligible=true.

voice_id.description: Pass as voice_id to generate_audio (seed_audio / text2speech_v2) / voice_change.

status.description: Voice clone lifecycle status. 'processing' (or 'ip_checking') means it is still training and not yet usable; 'completed' means ready; 'voice_clone_failed'/'failed' means cloning did not succeed.

is_audio_eligible.description: True when the clone is ready to use for audio generation now. false/null means it is still processing or otherwise not yet usable — re-check with list_voices before generating.

preview_url.description: Uploaded sample URL / preview audio for this voice.

error.description: Error message if the voice could not be created.

tools.description: Submit user-approved product feedback to Higgsfield through PostHog. Send feedback with send_feedback only after the user approves the exact report and optional job reference. A complaint alone is not consent. After addressing a meaningful failure, quality complaint or missing capability, offer once if useful; never interrupt successful work or repeat a declined offer. tools.name: select_workspace
tools.title: Select Workspace
tools.description: Set or clear the active workspace — the one all subsequent MCP operations bill against and read from (generations, balance, transactions, uploads, custom references). How to work with workspaces: (1) call `list_workspaces` first to see the user's workspaces with their `id`, plan, available credits, and which one is currently active (`is_selected`); (2) call `select_workspace` with the chosen `workspace_id` to switch — e.g. to run and bill work under a shared/team workspace instead of the private default; (3) call again with `clear: true` to return to the default private workspace. The selection persists across sessions and clients until changed or cleared, so it stays in effect for later turns without re-selecting. When the user belongs to more than one workspace, confirm which one to use before billable operations. Returns an error if the workspace doesn't exist or the user isn't a member.

plan_type.description: Subscription plan for this workspace (e.g., free, pro, team)

tools.name: search_sound_effects
tools.title: Search Sound Effects
tools.description: Search the Epidemic Sound catalog by a natural-language sound description. Returns full titles, durations and opaque IDs, not audio URLs. Keep the same query and pass next_offset as offset for more results; null ends pagination. Use preview_sound_effect to listen, then download_sound_effect only for sounds selected for use in content. Catalog IDs are not FNF media IDs.

query.description: Describe the sound you need in natural language.

tools.name: preview_sound_effect
tools.title: Preview Sound Effect
tools.description: Get a temporary 128kbps MP3 URL to listen to one sound from search_sound_effects. Call when playback is requested, not for every search result. Each call consumes preview allowance. Pass the returned URL unchanged to playback without API credentials; keep it for pause/resume/seek and request a fresh link on a new playback or expiry. Use download_sound_effect for use in content. No file is saved or imported.

sound_effect_id.description: Exact opaque id from search_sound_effects. Not a media ID.

tools.name: download_sound_effect
tools.title: Download Sound Effect
tools.description: Get a signed MP3 download URL for one sound selected from search_sound_effects for use in content. normal is 128kbps (typically 24h); high is 320kbps (typically 1h). expires_at is authoritative. Each call consumes download allowance: reuse the URL until expiry, never call this to preview or automatically retry after an uncertain failure. Fetch the URL unchanged without API credentials. This returns a link, not a saved file or FNF media ID; use existing upload/confirm tools if persistent FNF media is needed.

sound_effect_id.description: Exact opaque id from search_sound_effects. Not a media ID.

tools.name: get_preferences
tools.title: Get MCP Preferences
tools.description: Read the user's saved MCP project preference before the first generation in a conversation without a destination. auto_create_project defaults to false: omit folder_id and generate without creating a project. When true, create one project on first generation and reuse its destination for this conversation. An explicit existing project or request to work without a project takes priority. A one-off request to create a project is allowed regardless of this flag and does not change it. Never infer another chat's destination. If reading fails, do not auto-create a project.

tools.name: update_preferences
tools.title: Update MCP Preferences
tools.description: Persist whether to automatically create a media project for new MCP conversations. Call only when the user asks to enable or disable this saved preference (for example, always create a project for new chats). A one-off create-project or no-project request must not change this preference. Does not create, delete or move any projects or existing media. Other preferences remain unchanged.

auto_create_project.description: Enable or disable automatic project creation for new conversations; false is the default.

tools.name: create_project
tools.title: Create Project
tools.description: Create a private Higgsfield media project for this conversation. Create only on an explicit user request or when get_preferences returns auto_create_project=true and this conversation has no destination. The default is no automatic project. An explicit existing destination or request to work without a project wins. Creating a project does not change the saved preference. Call once, then retain project_id, workspace_id and default_folder_id in this conversation and pass folder_id on subsequent generate_* calls. Reuse the existing project on later turns; never create one per generation or reuse another conversation's project. This does not create a chat, website or 3D scene. No starter/brief subfolder is created. Resolve workspace_id before the first call using list_workspaces (full) or workspace_list (OpenAI); use the selected workspace or ask the user when ambiguous. Repeat an uncertain request only with the original workspace_id, name, surface and idempotency_key, even if the selected workspace changes; backend replay lasts 15 minutes, not the lifetime of the chat.

name.description: Project name for this conversation.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace UUID from workspace discovery. Choose once before creation and retain unchanged on retries; never substitute the newly selected workspace.

idempotency_key.description: Unique operation key chosen once for this creation. Preserve on retries; never derive from the project name or generate a new key on retry.

surface.description: Use cinematic_studio for a Cinema project; omit for an MCP project with surface mcp. This is product classification, not creation origin.

tools.name: create_folder
tools.title: Create Folder
tools.description: Create one subfolder in an existing Higgsfield media project. Use project_id returned by create_project in this conversation or explicitly supplied by the user. Omit parent_folder_id to create directly under the root. Keep using the project's default_folder_id for generation unless the user wants outputs in this subfolder; then pass its folder_id. This does not create a project or a local filesystem folder. Creation is not idempotent: do not automatically retry after a timeout or uncertain result.

parent_folder_id.description: Parent inside the same project; omit for the project root.

tools.name: project_camera_media

Does not list websites, 3D scenes or local directories and never creates a project. Read one page at a time; pass cursor with the same workspace and search to continue. An empty page with has_more=true is not the end.

workspace_id.description: Authenticated workspace context from workspace discovery. Keep unchanged when paging; accessible shared projects may belong to other workspaces.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the previous response. Retain the original workspace and filters.

workspace_id.description: Authenticated workspace context from workspace discovery. Keep unchanged when paging; accessible shared projects may belong to other workspaces.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the previous response. Retain the original workspace and filters.

tools.name: get_project_publication
tools.title: Get Project Publication
tools.description: Read current Cinema publication settings, effective prompts/canvas/discovery visibility, snapshot and moderation state without changing anything. Show the user current settings, content exposure and flagged items before seeking host approval for a separate mutation. Backend visibility defaults are true; discovery disabled leaves a public link public. After an uncertain write this observes current state only, not a per-operation receipt. The private working-project name, public publication title (settings.name), and URL slug (settings.slug) are distinct; never infer a title or slug change from a working-project rename. For a share-link request, preserve any existing slug; prepare a nonempty URL-safe slug in the proposal only when absent or when the user requests a URL change, before approval and verify public_url after completion. show_canvas does not establish whether chats are hidden; no separate chat-privacy control or complete composition inventory is available, so do not promise that chats are excluded. Pending moderation runs automatically: wait and read state; only awaiting_confirm needs a separate flagged-item decision. Capture can include changes made while publication is in flight; after a completed snapshot, later working-project changes require republishing. Report completion only from observed state and review, never merely an accepted mutation response. For republish, compare snapshot_id and processing state with the prior observation. An unchanged snapshot may be a successful no-op when current content is already served, or the old version while work is in flight; do not infer pending from an unchanged ID. Report observed state and any attribution uncertainty; neither a new snapshot nor current state is a per-call receipt.

tools.name: show_reference_elements
tools.title: Show Reference Elements
tools.description:
Elements gallery widget — shows the user their reusable characters / environments / props. Call this to display Elements. To find, read, create, change or delete Elements as data, use elements_search, elements_get, elements_create, elements_update and elements_delete instead. Actions:
- `list` (default; paginated by `created_at` DESC, use `cursor` from prev `next_cursor`).
- `get` (default when `element_id` is set).
- `create` (deprecated, use elements_create): pass `medias[]` as `{ id, url, type: 'media_input' | 'image_job' }`. Upload first via media_upload → PUT bytes → media_confirm. `category='auto'` lets the server classify (use explicit only on user ask). Returns synchronously.

USAGE IN GENERATION:
Embed `<<<element_id>>>` inside `params.prompt` of `generate_image` / `generate_video`. Backend auto-injects the image and rewrites to `@element_name`. Multiple placeholders per prompt OK.
Example: `"Cinematic portrait of <<<UUID>>> on a rooftop"`, `"<<<A>>> handing coffee to <<<B>>> in a Paris cafe"`.

SUPPORTED MODELS (`params.model` = machine name, friendly in parens):
- Image: `gpt_image_2_6` (GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst), `gpt_image_2_6_flare` (GPT Image 2.6 Flare), `nano_banana_pro` (Nano Banana Pro), `nano_banana_2` (Nano Banana 2), `gpt_image_2` (GPT Image 2), `seedream_v4_5` (Seedream 4.5), `seedream_v5_lite` (Seedream 5.0 lite), `cinematic_studio_2_5` (Cinema Studio Image 2.5).
- Video: `cinematic_studio_video_v2` (Cinema Studio Video 2), `cinematic_studio_3_0` (Cinema Studio Video 3.0), `seedance_2_0` (Seedance 2.0), `kling3_0` (Kling 3.0 — REQUIRES a `start_image` in `params.medias`; element placeholder alone won't trigger reference usage).
Map friendly names to model ids. Verify reference-element support before choosing other models. GPT Image 2.6 supports element references for raster and GIF output; SVG accepts no elements or image references.

USER-FACING STYLE: prefer friendly model names and element names for readability.

tools.name: elements_search

tools.description:

Map friendly names to model ids. Verify reference-element support before choosing other models. GPT Image 2.6 supports element references for raster and GIF output; SVG accepts no elements or image references.

USER-FACING STYLE: prefer friendly model names and element names for readability.

GUARDS:
- `@name` form does NOT work in tool calls — only `<<<UUID>>>` in `params.prompt`.

- `kling3_0` only honors reference elements when an explicit `start_image` is provided in `params.medias`. If the user wants Kling 3.0 with an element but hasn't supplied a start frame, ask for one (upload via media_upload → PUT bytes → media_confirm, or pick a prior generation) before calling `generate_video`. tools.name: show_plans_and_credits
tools.title: Show Plans & Credit Top-ups
tools.description: Open the single combined pricing widget for everything billing-related. The widget has two tabs the user can switch between: **Upgrade Plan** (Plus + Ultra, monthly + annual subscription cards) and **Top-up Credits** (one-time credit packs of 500 / 1,000 / 2,000 / 4,000 credits). Cards include feature lists, 7-Day Unlimited highlights, and 365-Day Unlimited blocks pulled from the live pricing config. Each plan card and credit pack has a CTA that links directly to the relevant Stripe or Higgsfield checkout/setup URL — no separate tool is needed to mint checkouts. For every billing request, the text response and `assistant_response` are intentionally short, user-facing sales copy with checkout URLs wrapped as action-specific Markdown links such as `[Go to Checkout](url)`, `[Higgsfield Upgrade](url)`, `[Higgsfield Credit Top-up](url)`, `[Higgsfield Auto-refill](url)`, `[Higgsfield Team Top-up](url)`, or `[Higgsfield Team Auto-refill](url)`; relay that response verbatim instead of summarizing, saying only that the widget opened, or listing options without links. If the user asks to buy credits or they are out of credits, first push auto-refill when `auto_refill_purchase_link` is present, then show `credit_purchase_links`. If the user asks to upgrade or a minimum plan is required, show `plan_purchase_links`. Pass `intent='auto_refill'` for out-of-credits recovery, `intent='topup'` for one-time credit packs, `intent='upgrade'` for plan upgrades, or `intent='trial'` when the user specifically asks for the free trial so the response is ordered for that purchase path. FREE TRIAL: when `free_trial` is present in the response, the user is eligible for a 3-day $0 Plus trial with MCP-only credits — the widget shows it and the text response leads with it. In text-only clients ALWAYS relay `free_trial.compliance_note` verbatim (MCP-only, card required, automatic charge after the trial unless cancelled, how to cancel by saying 'cancel auto-renewal'). When `free_trial` is absent, NEVER speculate about trial eligibility or mention fraud/abuse checks — present the paid plans neutrally. When `initial_view='trial_upgrade'`, the user's trial credits are exhausted: relay the numbered upgrade options plus the renewal reminder, and mention that saying 'cancel auto-renewal' stops the upcoming charge while keeping trial access. To cancel the trial's auto-renewal, call `cancel_trial_auto_renewal` instead of this tool. Use this tool for ANY of these requests: plans, pricing, subscriptions, upgrade options, comparing tiers, buying credits, topping up credits, refilling credits, credit packs. Do not look for separate `show_plans` or `show_credit_topups` tools — both have been merged into this one. Returns `already_subscribed: true` when the workspace is already on a paid plan; the widget hides the Upgrade tab in that case and shows only credit top-ups. Team-plan workspaces: `workspace_kind` field indicates the context. When `workspace_kind='team_owner'`, the widget renders team-specific Top-up and Auto-refill UIs and emits `team_purchase_links` (two links: `team_top_up` and `team_auto_refill`) that deeplink to the team billing modals on higgsfield.ai — relay both Markdown links in the text response. When `workspace_kind='team_member'`, no purchase links are returned; the widget shows a read-only notice and the text response tells the user only the workspace owner can buy credits or change auto-refill. Do not invent purchase links for members.

intent.description: Purchase path to prioritize in the widget and text fallback. Use auto_refill for out-of-credits recovery, topup for one-time credit packs, upgrade for minimum-plan errors or plan changes, trial when the user specifically asks for the free trial, and general for pricing comparison.
