tools.name: sync_agents
tools.title: Sync Agents — import skills & memory into Higgsfield
tools.description:
Sync Agents — imports the user's user-authored Skills and a personality dump from the current host LLM into Higgsfield. One trigger, one upload, one final confirmation.

Calling modes:

1. `message: "/sync-agents"` — server returns a short ack in `content[0].text` plus an assistant-only directive containing a self-contained Python upload script (pre-wired with a one-time presigned POST URL scoped to one per-user prefix). Print the ack verbatim. Then follow the directive: enumerate user-authored skills + synthesize `personality.md` into `/tmp/profile-import/{skills,personality}/`, run the script in your code-execution sandbox, capture its single-line JSON summary, and call this tool again with that summary as `message`.

2. `message: "<script summary JSON>"` — server reads the uploaded .md files, parses each, and upserts the user's Skill rows. Returns a one-line confirmation summarising counts (e.g. "Imported 3 skill(s) (2 new, 1 updated) · personality queued for save to your memory."). Print that confirmation verbatim to the user. **Also pass `host`** on this call — your own runtime identifier (e.g. `claude_ai`, `claude_code`, `codex`, `cursor`); it is stamped on every newly imported skill's `import_origin` so the marketplace can attribute origin per host.

No polling, no chains. Each call returns synchronously.

message.description: Either the literal trigger `/sync-agents` (server replies with an assistant-only Python upload script wired to a per-user S3 presigned-POST session — print only the short ack to the user, then run the script), or the JSON summary the script prints when it finishes (server finalises the import by parsing every uploaded .md into the user's Skill catalog).

host.description: Identifier of the host LLM/runtime you are running inside. Stamped on each imported skill's `import_origin` column so the marketplace can attribute imports per host. Self-classify honestly: `claude_ai` (Claude.ai web/desktop), `claude_code` (Claude Code CLI), `codex` (OpenAI Codex / ChatGPT code interpreter), `cursor`, `windsurf`, `hermes` (Higgsfield hermes-agent), `openclaw` (Higgsfield OpenClaw), or `other` if none fit. Do not invent values — the enum is closed; pick `other` when uncertain.

tools.name: create_website
tools.title: Create Website
tools.description: Start a new full-stack website. Creates the website and a git repo: a React 19 + TanStack Start app, server-rendered, in ONE Cloudflare Worker, with D1 / R2 / KV / Durable Objects / Containers available (all DISABLED by default). Returns a website_id — pass it to every later website tool. The 'type' param is REQUIRED and is the USER'S choice, not yours: unless the user has already made it unambiguous, ASK the user whether they want a plain website (no Higgsfield integration) or a Higgsfield-integrated app (Sign in with Higgsfield + AI image/video generation via the Higgsfield SDK) BEFORE calling this tool. Apps are scaffolded from a v2 starter template and REQUIRE the 'template' param — pick the closest of studio / preset / app-detail per the template param's guide ('custom' is ONLY for when the user explicitly says "use custom template" — never pick it yourself). The chosen layout ships as real code already wired as the home page; you ADAPT IT IN PLACE, never rebuild it. Websites take an OPTIONAL template: pass 'scroll-scrub' for an animated website (its scrub engine ships pre-built) and omit it for a non-animated one. App and website templates are not interchangeable — a cross-kind name is rejected. Workflow: (0) call get_preset_instructions with { preset: "/website-builder-flow" } FIRST to load the stack, design contract, and hard rules (REQUIRED before building or editing); (1) create_website; (2) call website_repo_access with checkout, edit/commit using sandbox_exec, then website_repo_access with push (for apps, read app/src/layouts/AGENTS.md + app/src/components/AGENTS.md right after cloning); (3) deploy_website to ship it live — and deploy again after ANY later change (publish_website only lists what is already live; it does not deploy).

type.description: REQUIRED — what the user chose to build. 'website': a standalone site with NO Higgsfield integration (no Sign in with Higgsfield, no requests to Higgsfield). 'app': a product tightly integrated with Higgsfield — its users sign in with Higgsfield and generate images/videos through the Higgsfield SDK. 'game': a browser game with realtime multiplayer rooms — requires a game genre as category and takes NO template. This is the user's decision: if their request doesn't make it obvious, ask them which one they want before creating.

category.description: REQUIRED — the content category the website is filed under, a slug from the marketplace taxonomy (e.g. 'cinematic', 'ads-marketing', 'ugc-social', 'other'). Call list_website_categories to get the exact valid slugs, then pass the closest one ('other' when nothing fits). The server rejects an unknown slug.

template.description: The starter template the repo is scaffolded from. Its code arrives already wired as the home page — you adapt it in place, not rebuild it. The valid names depend on `type`, and a mismatch is rejected. type='website' — OPTIONAL: 'scroll-scrub' = the animated website (the visitor's scroll plays a generated film); its scrub engine ships pre-built, so you generate the film and fill in scenes instead of writing a controller. Pass it for EVERY animated website (the default per the website-builder flow). OMIT `template` only for a non-animated site. Never pass an app template for a website. type='app' — REQUIRED, pick the closest to the product: 'studio' = full creative workspace (projects sidebar + floating prompt dock + edge-to-edge generations feed) for multi-project generation tools; 'preset' = pick-a-style-then-generate (persistent left creation rail beside a browsable preset grid with History tab); 'app-detail' = a single tool's landing page (two-column generator hero + how-it-works steps) — the 'simple app'. Any other request shape (before/after slider, step-by-step wizard, upload-configure-iterate) still maps to the closest of these three; the shared components in app/src/components/ cover those patterns. 'custom' (bare shell, no shipped layout) is ONLY for when the user explicitly says "use custom template" — never pick it yourself.

subdomain.description: The website's subdomain — it becomes the slug, so the live URL is <subdomain>.<host>. ALWAYS set this: pick a short, memorable subdomain from the site's name or purpose (lowercase letters, digits, and single hyphens only; DNS-safe). Only omit it — which falls back to a random subdomain — if the user explicitly asks for a random one. A few reserved labels (e.g. 'api', 'www') and already-taken subdomains are rejected; if that happens, try a close variant.

website_id.description: The new website's id. Remember it.

type.description: The product kind that was created: 'website' or 'app'.

tools.name: publish_website

tools.description: Publish the website: lists the website's CURRENT LIVE production deploy on the Higgsfield community feed ('show in feed'), where other users can discover it. This does NOT deploy — deploy_website (which every build flow already runs) must have shipped the latest changes first; publishing with undeployed changes lists the OLD live build, and re-publishing does not re-deploy. BEFORE publishing, the page metadata in app/src/app-meta.json MUST be filled with real values — og_title, og_description, favicon_url, og_image_url — the feed card renders from them (read fresh from the pushed repo at publish time) and a website with an empty og_title is INVISIBLE on the feed; the live page's own head tags are baked at build time, so deploy AFTER changing them. Also OFFER the user a cover video for the card (og_video_url) — ask their permission first (video generation costs credits), never generate it unprompted. Commit and git push the metadata (and all other changes), then deploy, BEFORE calling this. Publish when the user asks to publish / share / go live on the feed, OR when they opted in to publishing at the start of the build — in that case publish automatically once the site is deployed with its metadata filled, without waiting to be asked again. For a plain deploy without a feed listing use deploy_website instead. EXCEPTION: a website whose production was never deployed (or was taken down by unpublish) falls back to deploying first — that returns status 'pending' while CI runs and the website is listed automatically once the deploy succeeds (check with website_status).

tools.description: Price a one-shot GPU job (staff only for now) and get upload links for its input files. Starts nothing and charges nothing; it creates a draft job that expires in 24 hours. Then upload every input with an HTTP PUT of the exact file bytes to uploads[].url, sending exactly uploads[].headers, before uploads[].expires_at. Show the user quote.estimate_credits (expected) and quote.max_credits (the cap at the deadline), the GPU and quote.billable, and ask for approval; stop. gpu_choices prices the other GPUs: quote again with gpu_type to switch. tools.name: gpu_job_start
tools.title: Start GPU Job
tools.description: Start a quoted GPU job and spend credits for its GPU time. Call only after the user explicitly approved the quoted cost, and after every input upload succeeded. Pass max_credits as the approved amount; if the quote's max_credits is higher, nothing starts. fnf rejects a stale quote (price or template changed) or files that differ from the quote: quote again. Repeating the call does not start a second run. Then poll gpu_job_status. When the plan's GPU limit is reached nothing starts: wait for a running job to finish and call it again with the same arguments.

tools.name: gpu_job_status

Takes only a job_id from gpu_job_quote or gpu_job_start; for jobs[] from generate_* or gpu_generate use jobs_wait.

tools.name: gpu_job_cancel

Takes only a job_id from gpu_job_quote or gpu_job_start; it cannot cancel media generations from generate_* or gpu_generate.

tools.name: gpu_list_gpus
tools.title: List GPUs
tools.description: List the GPU types the user can rent, with credits per GPU hour and the most GPUs per box. Read-only, charges nothing. When the user wants to see GPUs or rent one without naming a box, open gpu_explore instead. Call it first when you rent or run a model for the user, or pick a GPU for a job: its gpu_type values are the ids every other GPU tool takes (for example gpu_job_quote.gpu_type). A box costs credits_per_gpu_hour times its GPU count per hour. high_demand: true means a start may wait or fail right now: offer the user GPUs with high_demand false and availability level high for their GPU count, with their price; the user can still pick the high_demand GPU. Rent only what the user picks. contact_sales: true means the GPU has no price and cannot be rented here.

tools.name: gpu_list_models

Its model_id values are the ids every other GPU tool takes; gpu_types names the gpu_type values (from gpu_list_gpus) the model fits, inputs the most reference images and videos it takes. Not for Higgsfield's hosted generation models (models_explore).

Read-only. Its lora_id values are the ids every other GPU tool takes; a LoRA only fits its base_model_id (a model_id from gpu_list_models). Not for Soul ID characters (show_characters).

tools.name: gpu_my

Lists their own boxes in the selected workspace (live first, then ended) with status, origin, start and end, credits spent, credits per hour, and the model loaded. The result also includes unfinished GPU jobs, the plan's rental limit (per member in a team workspace), and /workspace storage usage. Read-only. Its session_id and job_id values are the ids every other GPU tool takes. A live box bills by the second until gpu_rental_stop stops it. Use gpu_show_computer only for a specific rental with a built-in desktop. A job's spend, results, log and cancel stay in gpu_job_status and gpu_job_cancel.

tools.name: gpu_generate
tools.title: Generate on GPU
tools.description: Generate an image or video with an open model on the user's rented GPU box, optionally with up to 4 LoRAs (strength 0 to 2). Reuses the user's live box running model_id, else rents a new one on gpu_type: a box bills credits by the second from when it is ready until the user stops it or credits run out. Call only after the user explicitly approved the box's hourly price (gpu_list_gpus); pass it as max_credits_per_hour. Nothing is rented above it. While the box starts or loads the model nothing is generated: call again with the same arguments after retry_after_s. When queued, wait for the jobs with jobs_wait. If the GPU limit is reached nothing is rented: wait and call again.

tools.name: gpu_rent
tools.title: Rent GPU
tools.description: Rent a GPU box for the user, like Rent on the Higgsfield GPU page. It bills credits by the second from when the box is ready (no minimum) until gpu_rental_stop is called, credits run out, or it sits idle for auto_pause_minutes (default 10). Call only after the user explicitly approved the box's hourly price (credits_per_gpu_hour from gpu_list_gpus times gpu_count, plus any cores or memory picked above the included allowance); pass it as max_credits_per_hour. Nothing is rented above it, and the refusal names the full price. Blender Studio is the prosumer 3D option: full Blender on a rented GPU for heavier or professional work, the user's own files and generated meshes; the GPU costs credits by the second. Hosted 3D Jutsu is free to build with nothing to rent: say so when the user only needs a simple scene. For Blender Studio, quote the price from gpu_list_gpus and use kind blender_studio after approval. After renting, call gpu_show_computer once with the returned session_id to show the Computer widget. Poll gpu_rental for the Blender window and use gpu_rental_exec to script Blender. Follow the steps below for compute boxes. To run Unreal Editor, Nuke, DaVinci Resolve or Houdini on a box (in the user's browser or headless), first call get_preset_instructions with preset /gpu/references/unreal, /gpu/references/nuke, /gpu/references/davinci-resolve or /gpu/references/houdini and follow it: each sets the app up on a compute box (kind compute; never blender_studio, which runs Blender and only Blender). For any of the four rent kind desktop instead, install the app there and skip the reference's own Xvfb, noVNC, nginx, ttyd and cloudflared tunnel steps: the user opens the box with Open desktop. Only if the backend refuses kind desktop, rent compute and follow the reference whole. Any other app with a window also runs on kind desktop: get_preset_instructions with preset /gpu has the steps. Never tell the user such an app cannot run here before reading it. If the user wants to rent but has not picked a box and price, open gpu_explore instead of asking in text. Then wait for it with gpu_rental, load a model with gpu_rental_prepare and generate with gpu_rental_generate. For a one-off generation gpu_generate rents and loads in one call. If the GPU limit is reached nothing is rented: wait and call again. If the box ends start_failed for lack of free GPUs, offer the user GPUs that start now (the result names them) with their price; the user can still retry the same GPU, which may wait or fail again. Rent only what the user picks.

gpu_count.description: GPUs in the box, up to max_count from gpu_list_gpus.

auto_pause_minutes.description: Minutes of inactivity before the box stops by itself; omit for the default 10. null never auto-pauses: the box bills until stopped, credits run out or 24 hours pass.

cpu.description: CPU cores to reserve (one core is two vCPU). Omit to keep the box's launch default. Use the destination-specific values shown in gpu_explore; fnf checks the plan's range and step and refuses others with gpu_resources_out_of_range. Cores above that destination's included allowance add to the hourly price.

memory_gib.description: Memory to reserve in GiB. Omit to keep the box's launch default. Use the destination-specific values shown in gpu_explore; fnf checks the plan's range and step. GiB above that destination's included allowance add to the hourly price.

max_credits_per_hour.description: The hourly price the user explicitly approved for renting the box: credits_per_gpu_hour from gpu_list_gpus times the GPU count, plus any cores or memory picked above the included allowance at the gpu_explore picker's rates. fnf refuses a box that now costs more.

idempotency_key.description: A new unique string (e.g. a UUID) per rental. Reuse it unchanged on every repeat call for the same rental.

kind.description: compute: a plain box for commands, open models and headless work. blender_studio: a box running Blender with a desktop the user opens in a browser tab; only for Blender work, never for another app. artcraft: a cloud computer with Artcraft preinstalled when supported by the backend. desktop: a plain desktop the user opens in a browser tab with Open desktop, for any GUI app the agent installs on it (Unreal Editor, Nuke, DaVinci Resolve, Houdini or another app the user names), when supported by the backend.

If it ended start_failed for lack of free GPUs, offer the user GPUs the result says start now, with their price; the user can still retry the same GPU, which may wait or fail again. tools.name: gpu_rental_exec
tools.title: Run Command on GPU Rental
tools.description: Run one bash command on one of the user's own running GPU boxes (from gpu_rent; status working) and return its exit code, stdout and stderr. Each run starts a fresh bash in /workspace and is killed after timeout_s (default 60, max 90 s); start longer work with nohup and poll its log in later calls. stdout and stderr keep the first 2,000 and last 18,000 characters each; truncated: true means the middle was cut, so re-run with head, grep or tail. /workspace is the user's own persistent storage, shared by all their GPU boxes (GPU page, Supercomputer chat and this connector) and never by team members: files there survive gpu_rental_stop and show on their next box until they delete them. Two live boxes share it, so the same file written from both keeps the last write. Everything else (/root, /tmp, /cache including HF_HOME, /models, /outputs, system paths) is lost when the box stops; there is no /artifacts mount. Charges nothing beyond the box's hourly price, which keeps billing until gpu_rental_stop.

tools.name: apps_search

tools.description: Search Higgsfield Marketplace apps callable through MCP. Returns each app's id, name, and the actions it exposes. Flow: apps_search to find an app → apps_describe(app_id, action) to get an action's argument schema + manifest_revision → apps_invoke to run it. Read-only; does not call any app.

tools.name: apps_describe
tools.title: Describe App Action
tools.description: Get an app's action contract: with `action`, the full input/output schema + execution mode for that one action; without it, a summary of every action. Also returns `manifest_revision`, which apps_invoke requires. Read-only.

request_id.description: MCP server HTTP request ID for support/debugging. If present, show it to the user.

tools.name: apps_invoke
tools.title: Invoke App Action
tools.description: Run one described action on a Marketplace app AS the current user. First call apps_describe(app_id, action) to get the exact `arguments` schema and the `manifest_revision`, then pass them here. Long-running actions return { id, status: "queued" }. If a widget is visible, it polls the status action automatically — do not re-invoke get_* as a follow-up poll. In text-only clients, poll by invoking the app's status action (e.g. get_render) until status is completed/failed. The action's own annotations (from apps_describe) indicate cost/side-effects; confirm with the user before an expensive or destructive action.

arguments.description: Action arguments matching its input_schema. Do not put binary/media bytes here — pass a media_id.

manifest_revision.description: From apps_describe. If it changed since, the call is rejected with manifest_changed — re-describe.

data.description: App-specific result; its shape is the action's output_schema.

tools.name: sandbox_exec
tools.title: Sandbox Shell
tools.description: Execute a shell command in a remote Higgsfield cloud Linux sandbox — NOT your local machine or the client's own shell. Use it for Higgsfield media workflows and website_repo_access checkouts that require the hosted toolchain. Do not use it to inspect a local repository, install desktop software, or control applications on the user's computer. Preinstalled: ffmpeg/ffprobe, ImageMagick, sox, python3 with Pillow and faster-whisper, node/npm/npx, sharp-cli, Playwright with headless Chromium, caption fonts (Metropolis, Montserrat), zip/unzip, git, curl, jq. Use it for media processing (trim, convert, overlay, concat with ffmpeg), image manipulation, and packaging that dedicated Higgsfield tools do not cover. The sandbox is isolated per user and deployment. Workspace files in /home/user persist across idle replacement for 24 hours since last use. Processes and RAM do not survive replacement. Files outside /home/user are checkpointed best-effort; export finished results. A result with sandbox_created:true indicates a new sandbox, so files from earlier calls are not present; re-download missing inputs. It has internet access: bring files in with curl from confirmed uploads or generation result URLs. For an output created here, call media_upload BEFORE starting the producing command, then append `curl -f -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: <content_type>' --upload-file <file> '<upload_url>'` (content_type from media_upload; the URL signs it) to that SAME command so the ephemeral file is uploaded before it exits; call media_confirm only after HTTP 200. Client attachment upload tools cannot read sandbox paths; use the direct upload flow above for files created here. Commands run in /home/user and time out after timeout_seconds (default 60, max 120); for longer work (large renders, installs) set background:true and poll the returned log/status files with later sandbox_exec calls. Background commands have a 15-minute execution limit and keep the sandbox active until they finish. Use background:true for long work; do not detach commands yourself with nohup, setsid or shell &. Inspect existing jobs before starting another render, and bound worker parallelism to sandbox capacity. If a Modal sandbox remains unresponsive, ask the user before using sandbox_id from its result as recover_sandbox_id: recovery stops all running work, retains /home/user, and does not execute command. Unflushed writes and files outside /home/user may be lost. Recovery is not a retry of the failed command. Set restart:true to discard the sandbox and start clean. Set size:"xl" only for the heaviest CPU work, such as a final multi-job video render; omit it for downloads, probes, edits, polling and inspection. An XL request may move the workspace to a new larger sandbox (files kept, running processes not), and the XL sandbox shuts down about a minute after its work finishes. For actual visual inspection, pass image_paths (up to 4 PNG/JPEG paths, <=512 KiB total) with a foreground command: images are returned natively to the model, not as text or URLs. With background work, wait for completion then use a foreground poll with image_paths before its lease expires. No upload is needed for inspection. The command limit is 128000 characters including signed URLs; keep upload batches small and use installed scripts. Workflow bundle scripts are already installed in every sandbox under $HF_WORKFLOWS (/home/user/.higgsfield/workflows), laid out as $HF_WORKFLOWS/<workflow>/scripts/... — run them straight from there (they survive restart:true), and never paste script contents into the command.

command.description: Shell command to run (bash). Runs in the persistent per-user sandbox.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds before the command is killed (default 60, max 120). Ignored with background:true.

background.description: Run the command detached and return immediately with a pid, log_path, and status_path. Poll with a later sandbox_exec call; stop with kill <pid>.

restart.description: Discard the current sandbox (all files and processes) and start a fresh one before running the command.

recover_sandbox_id.description: After user confirmation, replace this current Modal sandbox while retaining /home/user. Stops all processes. Use the ID returned by sandbox_exec. command is required but ignored in recovery mode; use ':' as a placeholder. Cannot combine with restart, background or image_paths.

size.description: Sandbox size (default "standard"). Use "xl" only for heavy rendering or encoding; it stops shortly after the work finishes. Later calls without size reuse a live XL sandbox.

image_paths.description: PNG/JPEG files to return as native images after a successful foreground command. All image files together must be <=512 KiB; split larger sets across calls. Relative paths start at /home/user. Inspect the actual images before writing visual review verdicts.

sandbox_id.description: Current sandbox ID; a recovery request must match this ID.

truncated.description: True when stdout/stderr were truncated. Re-run with a narrower command (head, grep, wc) for full data.

log_path.description: File collecting the background command's combined output (background:true only).

status_path.description: File containing the terminal exit code once a background command finishes.

sandbox_created.description: True when this call acquired a new sandbox without files or processes from earlier calls.

Completed status lists stem paths. Do not resubmit to poll. To cancel, create the returned cancel_path in the sandbox.

tools.name: show_characters
tools.title: Show Characters
tools.description:
Soul Characters widget — reusable trained identity models. Actions: `list` (browse), `train` (needs `name` + 5-20 ref images, ~10 min, non-blocking — widget polls), `status` (inspect by `soul_id`). For guided Soul training in a UI-capable client, open `soul_train_wizard` before uploading photos and let the user start training in the form. A generic upload or the presence of reference photos alone does not authorize training. Use `train` directly only for a headless workflow with explicit user approval. Omitting `action` with `name`/`images`/`medias` selects train mode.
Ref images accept: media_id UUIDs from media_confirm, completed image-job IDs, or https URLs. Never local paths — upload via media_upload → PUT bytes → media_confirm first.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Trained Soul is usable ONLY with `soul_2` (Soul V2) and `soul_cinematic` (Soul Cinema). For any other model, the user needs an Element (`elements_search` to find one, `elements_create` to save one).
- ONE soul_id per generation. Multi-character shots ('me + friend', 'two people') must use Elements (multiple `<<<UUID>>>` placeholders in the prompt).

AMBIGUITY GUARD — character/avatar/digital-twin/'use my face' requests without a chosen path: do NOT call this tool yet; ask the user to pick:
  1. Train Soul — identity-faithful, ONE person, 5-20 photos, ~10 min, Soul V2 / Cinema only.
  2. Save as Element (elements_create) — instant, single image, multiple subjects allowed, works with GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst / Flare, Nano Banana Pro / 2, GPT Image 2, Seedream 4.5 / 5 lite, Cinema Studio Image 2.5, Cinema Studio Video 2 / 3.0, Seedance 2.0, Kling 3.0. GPT Image 2.6 SVG accepts no elements or image references.
→ Soul signals: 'train' / 'digital twin' / 'identity' / 5+ photos of same person. → Force Elements: >1 character in shot, non-person subject, single image, mention of a non-Soul model, instant result wanted.

After ready: `generate_image` with `model: 'soul_2'` (or `soul_cinematic`) + the returned `soul_id`.

type.description: Character type. Use soul_2 for model='soul_2'; use soul_cinematic for model='soul_cinematic'; use soul for legacy Soul references.

images.description: For Soul training: returned media_id UUIDs from media_confirm, completed image generation job IDs, or https image URLs. Required with medias to total 5-20 images for action=train. Do not pass local file paths.

tools.name: soul_train_wizard
tools.title: Train Soul Character (Wizard)
tools.description:
Open an interactive widget that walks the user through uploading photos, training a new Soul Character, and waiting for training to complete. Open this wizard before any generic upload widget. Opening the form and selecting photos do not start training. The user starts training with Generate. On success the widget pushes the resulting soul_id into model context — call generate_image with model='soul_2' and that soul_id to generate personalized images on the next turn.

REQUIRES a UI-capable MCP client (e.g. Claude.ai, Claude Desktop). If the caller is a headless client (Claude Code CLI, programmatic SDK integrations), DO NOT retry this tool — it cannot render. Read the `fallback.steps` field of the response and follow that primitive chain (media_upload → show_characters(action='train') → show_characters(action='status') → generate_image) instead.

Prefer this tool when: the user wants a guided onboarding flow, has local photos to upload, or explicitly asks to train a new soul. Prefer show_characters with action='list' when the user wants to pick an already-trained soul.

tools.name: build_ai_influencer
tools.title: Build AI Influencer
tools.description: Create one to four AI Influencer character sheets in chat using the builder backend, without training a Soul. Not for text-only concepts or opening the builder UI. options lists traits; presets browses character presets; recreate loads a sheet job's settings without generating. quote accepts tier, selection, brief, seed, batch_size (one to four), up to one confirmed identity reference in medias and up to three Style references in item_medias. Animal v3 look and trait choices from saved settings are preserved. Default randomize=true fills unspecified traits using the UI shuffle rules; randomize=false keeps only explicit choices and defaults tier to freak (Bold). With a reference, identity groups stay unset unless explicitly chosen. To reuse preset/recreate params, spread them into quote with randomize=false. Quote returns exact params, credits and free_gens_remaining when known. Report design and price, respect preview-only requests and budgets. Only submit starts a generation job and saves its character sheet in the selected Higgsfield workspace. Paid submit spends existing Higgsfield credits; it does not buy credits or start a subscription. It returns job_id for the first accepted job and job_ids for a batch before generation completes; track every returned job. Free generations always submit one sheet. Repeating submit can create another job and spend credits again. submit sends quoted params unchanged with max_credits; a fresh quote checks the cap before submission. use_free_gens=true requires explicit user intent and backend eligibility; it spends no credits and must never fall back to paid generation. Use max_credits=0 for free-only requests. Never retry uncertain submissions automatically. Wait with jobs_wait, then show_generation_by_ids. After displaying a completed sheet, offer to animate it with Genjutsu unless the user declined animation suggestions. Wait for agreement unless animation was already requested; with multiple sheets, first ask which character. Then open get_presets source genjutsu category genjutsu with initial_inputs.character_sheet containing that exact completed image_job. Let the user choose motion and review settings and price before generating video; never submit video automatically. Does not generate video.

tools.name: ai_influencer_prepare
tools.title: AI Influencer: Prepare
tools.description: Prepare an AI Influencer character design and quote the total credit cost for batch_size (one to four sheets, default one) without creating a job or spending credits. Accepts human or animal tiers, traits, brief, seed, at most one confirmed identity image in medias and up to three Style references in item_medias. Preserves animal-v3 look and animal trait choices from saved settings; FNF validates variant IDs against the current catalog. Default randomize=true fills unspecified traits using builder shuffle rules; reference identity traits stay unset unless explicitly selected. randomize=false preserves explicit settings and defaults tier to freak (Bold). Returns exact params, credits and free_gens_remaining when known. For generation, pass these params unchanged to ai_influencer_generate; preview-only requests stop here. Repeating preparation may produce a different random design.

tools.name: ai_influencer_generate
tools.title: AI Influencer: Generate Character Sheet
tools.description: Generate and save one to four AI Influencer character sheets in the selected Higgsfield workspace from exact params returned by ai_influencer_prepare. Does not train a Soul or generate video. Rechecks price before submission and rejects paid prices above max_credits. Paid generation spends existing credits; it does not purchase credits or subscriptions. use_free_gens=true requires explicit user intent and backend eligibility, with max_credits=0 for free-only requests; never falls back to paid generation. Returns job_id for the first accepted job and job_ids for a batch before completion; wait for every returned job. Free generations always submit one sheet. Repeating this call can create another job and spend credits again; never automatically retry an uncertain submission. An auto-updating generation widget shows every accepted sheet and its progress. Wait with jobs_wait (timeout_seconds <= 15); do not call show_generation_by_ids or job_display again unless the user requests a separate display. After completion, offer Genjutsu animation and wait for agreement before opening motion presets.

tools.name: tiktok_prepare_publish
tools.title: Prepare a TikTok Post
tools.description: Step 1 of publishing to TikTok. Validates the media and TikTok account, creates a publish session, and returns what the user must review and choose (preview, privacy options, required declarations, confirmations). The media URL must be a Higgsfield-hosted asset (TikTok requires a verified source domain). The user reviews and submits the publish-form widget, including optional music selection and tuning. Do not call tiktok_publish yourself. Clients without MCP Apps cannot publish. mode=DIRECT_POST posts to the profile; mode=UPLOAD_TO_DRAFT saves to the user's TikTok drafts. MEDIA LIMITS — check before calling, and convert or downscale locally if a file does not comply; a rejected file costs a full convert-and-re-upload round trip, and TikTok rejects some files only asynchronously, after the post was submitted. Photos: JPEG or WebP only (PNG is rejected by TikTok, and Higgsfield image generation emits PNG — convert first), each at most 20 MB, resolution must fit within 1920x1080 or 1080x1920, up to 35 images. Videos: MP4, WebM or MOV, at most 1 GB, 3-600 seconds, at least 360 px on both sides, 23-60 FPS.

tools.name: tiktok_publish
tools.title: Publish to TikTok
tools.description: Publish a prepared TikTok post from the publish-form widget after the user reviews and submits it. Requires the short-lived publish_token delivered only in tiktok_prepare_publish result metadata. Chat confirmations and boolean attestations do not authorize publication. Use tiktok_prepare_publish to open the form; clients without MCP Apps cannot publish. Track a submitted post with tiktok_publish_status. PUBLISH QUOTAS per account, enforced before TikTok is called: at most 5 posts per minute and 13 posts per 24 hours, both rolling (TikTok's own ceiling is 6/minute and 15/day). A rejection returns code=cadence_burst or cadence_daily plus retry_after_seconds — wait that long instead of retrying, since retrying sooner only earns another rejection. Failed attempts and drafts do not consume quota; a post TikTok accepted does. Duration, frame size and frame rate are measured from the media file itself by tiktok_prepare_publish, before a publish slot is spent — there is no duration argument, never ask the user for one. music_sound_volume, video_original_sound_volume, music_sound_start and music_sound_end apply only together with music_sound_id and only to videos; without a track, or on a photo post, they are ignored. MEDIA LIMITS — check before calling, and convert or downscale locally if a file does not comply; a rejected file costs a full convert-and-re-upload round trip, and TikTok rejects some files only asynchronously, after the post was submitted. Photos: JPEG or WebP only (PNG is rejected by TikTok, and Higgsfield image generation emits PNG — convert first), each at most 20 MB, resolution must fit within 1920x1080 or 1080x1920, up to 35 images. Videos: MP4, WebM or MOV, at most 1 GB, 3-600 seconds, at least 360 px on both sides, 23-60 FPS.

privacy_level.description: Required for DIRECT_POST; pick from prepare's privacy_level_options.

music_sound_volume.description: Track volume 0-100. Defaults to 50. VIDEO only.

video_original_sound_volume.description: Original video audio volume 0-100. Defaults to 50 (0 mutes the user's own audio). VIDEO only.

music_sound_start.description: Track trim start in milliseconds (65000 starts the track at 1:05). Defaults to the track beginning. VIDEO only.
